newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses hit records on stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses hit records on stronger dollar.

text.p: Major European bourses all hit new peaks in early trading on Wednesday, encouraged by a stronger dollar and a growing conviction that interest rates would remain steady.

On foreign exchanges, the dollar strengthened against the mark and was trading just off its four-year high against the yen. But the mark was firmer against European currencies on a press report that Italy would be offered a compromise deal on EMU entry.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks surged to a new record of 4286.9 points on the FTSE index as investors became convinced that a meeting between finance minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George would leave interest rates unchanged.
Traders were also hopeful that a session of the U.S. central bank's policy making committee would not up rates. The Federal Open Markets committee makes its announcement at 1915 GMT tonight.

The mood was also cheered by a strong close on Wall Street on Tuesday. The Dow, down around 22 points when London markets closed, finished with a 27 point advance at the end of the first day of the FOMC meeting.
"Of course, we're also sitting tight ahead of the FOMC decision," one trader said.

Recent economic statistics in the U.S. continue to show non-inflationary growth whilst in the UK economists expect Chancellor of the Exchequer Clarke to continue to resist a rate rise at such a politically-sensitive time. The British government has to call a general election by late May.
In Frankfurt, shares climbed by 1.3 percent, lifted by Wall Street's positive close on Tuesday and the strength of the dollar trading above 1.64 marks, which was soon as boosted export prospects.

"There is strong support there from the dollar and the focus is very much on individual stocks, although the chemical sector is strong because of the dollar. The specific interest this morning is on Lufthansa," said one trader.
The DAX index of leading shares reached a trading record of 3090.52 points in early deals, eclipsing the high set only on Tuesday, before falling back slightly.

In Paris, French stocks rebounded on Wednesday, helped by firmness in bond prices and the franc, traders said. The CAC 40 index hit a trading high of 2535.78 points in early trade before slipping slightly.
On currency markets, the dollar was expected to remain bullish against the yen and any decision on interest rates by the FOMC would notmake much difference to dollar bulls, analysts said.
But the dollar and mark were locking horns after mark sentiment was boosted by a report that Italy will be offered a deal that would delay its entry into EMU.

The report, in Wednesday's Financial Times newspaper, quoted unnamed senior monetary officials saying Italy would be offered a "face-saving compromise" deal, which could be extended to Spain and Portugal, that would delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001.

"It's clear questions are being raised about Italy and Spain joining EMU in the first round. The mark is going to benefit as a result of those questions, as there will be flows out of the peripheral markets into the mark and mark assets for safety reasons," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
But analysts saw little chance of the dollar's underlying bullishness against the mark abating.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6475 marks and 123.25 yen after closing in Europe at 1.6424 marks and 122.30 yen on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was 22.6 points higher at 4,283.5.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 31.31 points higher at 3,098.08.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 30.25 at 2,533.60.
PRECIOUS METALS - Gold was fixed at $343.15 an ounce after closing in Europe on Tuesday at $346.30.
